name: Deliverable
description: Originally pure Veridian-Holt internal management jargon meaning 'a promised outcome or product due by a deadline,' the word escaped corporate channels around 2196 when Tier 3 contract workers began using it sarcastically to describe any promise made by someone with power over them. 'Your deliverable' became a cutting way to remind someone of an unfulfilled obligation — especially a debt, a favor owed, or a broken personal commitment. By 2210 it had spread to Tier 1 as heavy irony: on the Shelf, calling something someone's 'deliverable' implies they will never actually deliver it. The word now carries a bitter, knowing weight that its boardroom origins never intended.
cultural_impact: The term has become a linguistic marker of class awareness — how you use 'deliverable' signals whether you see corporate language as neutral, ironic, or hostile. Shelf residents using it heavily underline the gap between what institutions promise and what they actually provide, making it a quiet political act embedded in everyday speech.
key_figures: Priya Asante-Wojcik (labor organizer who popularized ironic usage)
Cass Mbuyi-Larsson (satirist, The Shelf Wire broadcast)
locations: The Shelf Wire broadcast hub, Tier 1 District 3
Mid-Meridian contract worker cafeterias, Tier 2-3 boundary
story_hooks: A Tier 3 union rep uses 'deliverable' in a negotiation with a Veridian-Holt executive who genuinely doesn't realize the term has become a slur for corporate broken promises — the miscommunication escalates dangerously.
Someone on the Shelf is calling in a very old 'deliverable' from a Tier 5 fixer — a promise made twenty years ago that the fixer assumed was forgotten.

A journalist investigating Veridian-Holt discovers the word's ironic spread was not accidental — a disgruntled internal employee deliberately seeded the satirical usage through anonymous Underworld channels.
definition: A promise or obligation owed, used with heavy irony to imply the person who owes it will never fulfill it; originally neutral corporate jargon that accumulated bitter class meaning as it spread downward through tiers.
usage_example: 'Oh sure, Helion said clean water infrastructure by 2215 — that's a real deliverable right there.'
spread: Universal across all tiers, but meaning shifts dramatically by tier — sincere in Tier 4-5, increasingly ironic and bitter from Tier 3 downward
